facts.text: The operational design domain (ODD) is the written description of the conditions under which a system is designed to work; an operating-domain taxonomy is the organized list of attributes used to write that description.
facts.quote: The operational design domain is the written description of the conditions under which a system is designed to work, and an operating-domain taxonomy is the organized list of attributes used to write it.

facts.text: An ODD specifies the environmental and operating conditions under which a safety claim is intended to hold, with explicit in-domain and out-of-domain boundaries.
facts.quote: It answers "under what environmental and operating conditions is the safety claim intended to hold?", with explicit in-domain and out-of-domain boundaries [Chapter 9].

facts.text: An example ODD for the braking system limits operation to reverse motion at 3 to 15 km/h in surface mines and quarries, with daylight or site lighting and no snow.
facts.quote: For the braking system, the ODD might say: reverse motion only, 3 to 15 km/h, surface mines and quarries, daylight and site lighting, no snow.

facts.text: The braking system's safety claim does not cover conditions outside its ODD, and the system should recognize when it has left that domain.
facts.quote: Anything outside is not claimed, and the system should know when it has left the domain.

facts.text: ISO 34503:2023 and ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0 formalize ODDs for automated road vehicles; both are scoped to automated road vehicles and have lanes and junctions as default attributes.
facts.quote: Both are scoped to automated road vehicles, and their default attributes are lanes and junctions.

facts.text: ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0, dated 3 April 2025, provides a machine-readable, technology-independent data model with restrictive definitions specifying what is allowed and permissive definitions specifying what is excluded.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0 (3 April 2025), which gives a machine-readable, technology-independent data model with restrictive definitions (what is allowed) and permissive ones (what is excluded) [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Off-road operating-domain taxonomies exist only as academic proposals, including a 2022 adaptation to underground mining and a 2024 adaptation to unstructured environments.
facts.quote: Off-road taxonomies exist only as academic proposals: one adapts the concepts to underground mining (2022), another to unstructured environments (2024)

facts.text: A 2025 agricultural operating-domain framework identifies the mining industry's EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) performance requirement PR-5A as a replicable model.
facts.quote: an agricultural framework (2025) names the mining industry's EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) performance requirement PR-5A as a replicable model [Chapter 9].

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: The off-road standard ISO 17757:2019 uses the notion of a "defined functional environment," which is related to an ODD.
facts.quote: The off-road standard ISO 17757:2019 uses the related notion of a "defined functional environment" [Chapter 1].

facts.text: For a job-site operating-domain taxonomy, the booklet proposes branches covering site and scenery (pit, quarry face, stockpile, haul route, workshop; berms, drop-offs, ruts); machine operating state (forward, reverse, articulating, swinging, loaded or unloaded); machine geometry (footprint, sensor height and pitch, occluding structures); objects (worker posture and clothing, light vehicle, machine, rock, low or buried object); relative interaction (crossing, emerging from occlusion, backing toward an object); weather and air, including dust; illumination; surface and braking (grade, gravel, mud, ice); sensor state; and human and system state.
facts.quote: The booklet proposes branches for a job-site program: site and scenery (pit, quarry face, stockpile, haul route, workshop; berms, drop-offs, ruts); machine operating state (forward, reverse, articulating, swinging, loaded or unloaded);

facts.text: The booklet recommends treating operating-domain categories as attributes rather than as 100 or more unrelated site names, so tests cover equivalence classes and attribute interactions instead of repeating sites.
facts.quote: The decisive design choice is to treat these as attributes rather than as 100 or more unrelated site names.

facts.text: Two differently named quarries can share the same safety-relevant attributes: rough terrain, dust, bright sun, metal clutter, an 8% grade and frequent crossings.
facts.quote: Two quarries with different names may share the same safety-relevant attributes (rough terrain, dust, bright sun, metal clutter, an 8% grade, frequent crossings)

facts.text: The ODD defines test coverage and must be written first, in October 2026, before scenarios, sites or sample sizes can be planned.
facts.quote: The ODD defines what "coverage" means, so it must be written first, in October 2026, before scenarios, sites or sample sizes can be planned [Chapters 1, 9].

facts.text: The ODD defines the narrow first release of the off-road braking system and the gates by which its operating domain widens.
facts.quote: It also defines the narrow first release and the gates by which it widens

facts.text: Every fielded off-road braking product launched with a narrow operating domain, such as reverse-only operation at 3 to 15 km/h.
facts.quote: every fielded off-road braking product launched with a narrow domain, such as reverse only at 3 to 15 km/h [Chapter 1].
